comparisons.comparison: Both firms disclosed new Board authorizations for common stock repurchase programs in 2024. Goldman Sachs disclosed a $30 billion program approved in 2023, whereas Bank of America authorized a new $25 billion program effective August 1, 2024, replacing its previous program. While the topic is identical (new repurchase authorization), the authorized amounts differ ($30 billion vs $25 billion) and the effective timing differs (2023 approval vs 2024 effective date).

comparisons.peer_topic: Shareholder Returns and Capital Repurchase Program
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi returned $6.7 billion to shareholders in 2024 via dividends and repurchases, and authorized a new $20 billion multiyear repurchase program in January 2025 with $1.5 billion planned for Q1 2025, subject to regulatory capital uncertainty.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclosed repurchase authorizations and activities, but with significant differences in timing and magnitude. Goldman Sachs reported a $30 billion program approved in 2023. Citigroup disclosed repurchases of $2.5 billion in 2024 and a new $20 billion multiyear program authorized in January 2025 (post-filing period relative to 2024 operations, but disclosed in 2024 filing). Citigroup's 2024 repurchase spend ($2.5 billion) was significantly lower than JPMorgan's or BAC's, and the new authorization amount ($20 billion) is lower than Goldman's ($30 billion).

sentences.text: In 2023, the Board approved a share repurchase program authorizing repurchases of up to $30 billion of our common stock.

• Citi returned $6.7 billion to common shareholders in the form of dividends ($4.2 billion) and share repurchases ($2.5 billion) in 2024. As previously disclosed, on January 13, 2025, Citigroup's Board of Directors authorized a new, multiyear $20 billion common stock repurchase program, with planned repurchases of $1.5 billion during the first quarter of 2025, subject to market conditions and other factors. After the first quarter of 2025, Citi will continue to assess the level of common share repurchases on a quarter-by-quarter basis given uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements, among other factors.

comparisons.peer_topic: New Common Share Repurchase Program Authorization
comparisons.peer_summary: On June 28, 2024, the Board authorized a new $30 billion common share repurchase program effective July 1, 2024, replacing the previous $30 billion program authorized in April 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase authorized new $30 billion share repurchase programs in 2024 to replace prior authorizations. Goldman's program was approved in 2023 with no set expiration, while JPMorgan's new program was authorized on June 28, 2024, effective July 1, 2024, replacing a previous $30 billion program from April 2022. Both companies maintain a $30 billion authorization magnitude, though the timing and expiration specifics differ.
